content:
Anyone ever play Elevator Saga? It's a cute elevator scheduler algorithm game.

Of course any sane human would want to play it in their Lean infoview. So.. now with the help of Claude, you can. Here's EleanvatorSaga:

output.mp4

Have fun :)

(n.b. I have not fully playtested it, I've played basically the first 3 levels just to confirm whether roughly the same simple algorithms solve the levels in Lean, but it's possible there are still some physics bugs to work out! Also shout out to Jovan Gerbscheid since an original reason to have Claude do this was to stress test RefreshComponent in lean.nvim :D)

Hahaha yes Julian this is so epic. The Lean infoview might become my new favorite game engine.

Now I just need to learn how to use Neovim...

This is amazing! (I was just playing elevator saga and I was anoyed about having to debug javascript code and then i remembered I saw a post about it in the lean zulip... finally I can play elevator saga in a proper programming language :grinning: ). Actually, it would be great to have a web version of this (maybe on the lean game server.

Please feel very encouraged to help make your dreams become reality :) -- I am very unlikely to have more time to work on it at this point (including having Claude work on it on our behalf) but contributions would be very welcome.

I was just looking around zulip and it doesn't seem like there is a working wasm build for a recent lean version. What is actually happening when #play is ran? I am trying to understand if this would work in an enviroment like the lean-webeditor where lean lives on a server and the client only edits the file in a browser (which of course introduces a lot of delay).

I believe it should work in a browser, the short version -- which you're getting as I'm about to jump on a train -- is "svgs are generated and then repeatedly refreshed as HTML components via RefreshComponents which comes from Proofwidgets)" (though I'm not sure the entirety of the lean4game setup would, which I think is what's required to get it on the game server, that I think has stronger constraints on the structure of a project)
